sheet-1.description: The lower half of sheet 1 of the Magnolia atlas of March 1925, drawn at 100 feet to the inch below a heavy line that separates it from the title, key, index, notes and key map in the upper half. It covers the south-western corner of the borough: Evesham Avenue along the top, Monroe, Adams and Washington Avenues across the middle, and the blocks south of Washington Avenue to the borough limit with Clementon Township, between Albertson Avenue on the west and the Philadelphia and Reading Railroad and Atlantic Avenue on the east. Walnut Avenue and Chestnut Avenue run north to south; Chestnut Avenue is marked not opened between Monroe and Adams Avenues, as are Adams Avenue west of Albertson and a strip west of Albertson. West Atlantic Avenue runs diagonally beside the railroad, which crosses the right edge of the sheet. The blocks are platted in regular house lots with consecutive house numbers, and are thinly built up with one and two storey frame dwellings, sheds and coops, most of them along Evesham, Monroe and Adams Avenues. A large lot west of Albertson Avenue at the left edge holds a single dwelling. Four-inch and six-inch water pipes are drawn along the streets with fire hydrants at the corners. The left margin is the borough limit with Gloucester Township. The map overlaps sheet 3 along Evesham Avenue and sheet 2 along the railroad and Atlantic Avenue.
notes: Modern names: Albertson Avenue South, Walnut Avenue South, Monroe/Adams/Washington Avenue West, Evesham Avenue West; West Atlantic Avenue is Atlantic Avenue Southwest and Atlantic Avenue is Atlantic Avenue Southeast.
The key map in the upper half (600 ft to the inch) is not part of this annotation's mask.

Top half: title, key, index, notes and a key map at 600 ft (not configured). Bottom half below the heavy line: map at 100 ft, Evesham Av to Washington Av between Albertson Av and the P. & R. R.R. (Atlantic Av). One part (mask below the line at y 4372).

sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 of the Magnolia atlas of March 1925, at 100 feet to the inch, covers the southern part of the borough east of the railroad. Evesham Avenue runs along the top with the stubs of Camden Avenue and Gill Street north of it. Below it Monroe, Adams, Washington, Lafayette and Jefferson Avenues run east from Atlantic Avenue and Warrick Avenue, crossed by Gloucester Avenue and, at the east, Cumberland Avenue. The Philadelphia and Reading Railroad (Atlantic City line) crosses the western part of the sheet diagonally between West Atlantic Avenue and Atlantic Avenue. Buildings of note are the Magnolia Evangelical Lutheran Church and Magnolia Borough Hall on Evesham Avenue, and the Adams Avenue Public School, a brick building at Adams Avenue and Warrick Avenue. The rest is a thin scatter of one and two storey frame dwellings, poultry houses, coops and sheds on long narrow lots; the block east of Gloucester Avenue and north of Washington Avenue (block 39) is open. Lafayette Avenue west of Warrick Avenue and part of Jefferson Avenue are marked not opened. The borough limit with Clementon Township crosses the lower part of the sheet; south of it, at the bottom right corner, a detached strip shows Magnolia Avenue and Wilbur Avenue with one dwelling. Water pipes and hydrants are drawn along the main streets.
notes: Warrick Av is modern Warwick Road South (spelling differs). Monroe, Adams, Washington and Evesham Avenue east of Warrick are modern ... Avenue East, west of it ... Avenue West.
Gill St is modern Gloucester Avenue north of Evesham.
Magnolia Avenue / Wilbur Avenue was accepted with a 4.0 m residual; the same junction was rejected on sheet 6.

100 ft. Evesham Av south to Jefferson Av, from W. Atlantic Av east to Cumberland Av; Warrick (Warwick Road South), Gloucester; detached corner at bottom right (Magnolia Av, Wilbur Av), drawn in place. One part.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 of the Magnolia atlas of March 1925, at 100 feet to the inch, covers the north-western part of the borough west of the railroad. Albertson Avenue and Walnut Avenue run north from Evesham Avenue, crossed by Madison, Jackson, Lincoln and Brooke Avenues, and West Atlantic Avenue runs beside the Philadelphia and Reading Railroad along the right side. East of the tracks, Atlantic Avenue and the ends of Lincoln, Jackson and Madison Avenues are shown. The blocks between Evesham and Brooke Avenues are platted in regular lots with consecutive house numbers and are well built up with one and two storey frame dwellings, sheds and coops. Buildings of note are Christ Protestant Episcopal Church on Walnut Avenue near Evesham Avenue, the Spiegle Brothers plumbing and heating shop at West Atlantic and Evesham Avenues, a milk station on the row of lots west of Albertson Avenue, and at the railroad the Magnolia station, a freight house and coal piles. North of Brooke Avenue the land is open, divided into a few large tracts with scattered houses and sheds, and block 51 west of Albertson Avenue is mostly empty. Water pipes with hydrants are drawn along Evesham, Madison, Jackson, Lincoln and Brooke Avenues. The sheet overlaps sheet 1 along Evesham Avenue and sheet 4 along the railroad.
notes: Brooke Av is modern Brooks Avenue; OpenStreetMap also has a Brooke Avenue farther north.

Albertson and Walnut Av are modern North Albertson Avenue and Walnut Avenue North; West Atlantic Av is Northwest Atlantic Avenue; Atlantic Av east of the tracks is Atlantic Avenue Northeast; Madison Av is Madison Avenue West.
100 ft. Brooke (Brooks Avenue today), Lincoln, Jackson, Madison Avs to Evesham Av, Albertson to the railroad; Magnolia Station. One part.

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 of the Magnolia atlas of March 1925, at 100 feet to the inch, covers the northern part of the borough east of the railroad. The Philadelphia and Reading Railroad runs down the left edge between West Atlantic Avenue and Atlantic Avenue. East of it, Lincoln, Jackson and Madison Avenues run across to Warrick Avenue, crossed by Camden Avenue, and Evesham Avenue runs along the bottom to Gloucester Avenue at the lower right, where Gill (an arbitrary name) runs north. White Horse Pike crosses the top right corner, with a garage and a few dwellings, and Warrick Avenue runs diagonally up to it. The built-up blocks between Lincoln and Evesham Avenues hold one and two storey frame dwellings with sheds, coops and poultry houses, and three public buildings: the Magnolia Baptist Church on Lincoln Avenue, the fire department on Jackson Avenue and the Lincoln Avenue Public School near Warrick Avenue. North of Lincoln Avenue the large block 50 is open land, and east of Warrick Avenue blocks 45 and the lots along White Horse Pike are only partly built. Four-inch water pipes and hydrants are drawn along the streets. The sheet overlaps sheet 3 along the railroad, sheet 2 along Evesham Avenue and sheet 5 along Warrick Avenue and White Horse Pike.
notes: Warrick Av is modern Warwick Road North; Atlantic Av is Atlantic Avenue Northeast; Gill is modern Gloucester Avenue north of Evesham Avenue.
100 ft. East of the railroad: Atlantic, Camden, Warrick Avs, Lincoln, Jackson, Madison to Evesham; White Horse Pike at top right; large open block 50. One part.

sheet-5-1.description: The main part of sheet 5 of the Magnolia atlas of March 1925, at 100 feet to the inch, covers the eastern part of the borough along White Horse Pike, from its junction with Warrick Avenue at the top left down to Evesham Avenue at the bottom. A heavy line cuts off the upper right corner, which holds a separate inset. White Horse Pike is lined on both sides with frame dwellings, a garage, greenhouses and a potting house, and with the Magnolia Inn near the top and Mechanics Hall farther south; New Ashland Road runs east from the Pike with a row of dwellings. Along Evesham Avenue at the bottom are the Magnolia Methodist Episcopal Church near Gill (an arbitrary name) and Gloucester Avenue, and further east a row of houses near Pincus (an arbitrary name) and King Street. Most of the area east of the Pike (blocks 46, 47 and 50) is open land divided into large irregular tracts, crossed by the borough limit with Centre Township, which runs diagonally from the upper middle toward the right edge. Six-inch water pipes run along White Horse Pike and Evesham Avenue. The sheet overlaps sheet 4 to the west, sheet 6 to the south and sheet 2 at the bottom left.
notes: New Ashland Rd is modern Ashland Avenue; Warrick Av is Warwick Road North; Gill is Gloucester Avenue; Pincus is modern King Street North.
Only five street junctions; scale and rotation are poorly fixed by the part's own control.

100 ft. Part 1: White Horse Pike from Warrick Av to Evesham Av, New Ashland Rd (Ashland Avenue), Gill and Pincus (arbitrary names). Part 2: inset above the heavy line, White Horse Pike, Warrick Av and Lapierre Av at Davis Rd (borough's north end, 'See Map of Barrington').

sheet-5-2.description: An inset in the upper right corner of sheet 5 of the Magnolia atlas of March 1925, at 100 feet to the inch, separated from the main map by a heavy line. It shows the northern tip of the borough, where White Horse Pike and Warrick Avenue run north to Davis Road, the boundary with Barrington, with Lapierre Avenue running east from Warrick Avenue. Block 49 between the Pike and Warrick Avenue holds a few dwellings, and block 48 east of Warrick Avenue a row of dwellings and outbuildings on narrow lots along Warrick and Lapierre Avenues. A note at the top reads 'See Map of Barrington' for the area beyond Davis Road, and the borough limit with Centre Township runs diagonally along the right side. A six-inch water pipe runs along White Horse Pike. The inset lies just north of the main part of the sheet, where Warrick Avenue crosses White Horse Pike.
notes: Warrick Av is modern Warwick Road North. The street index spells it La Pierre Ave.
Placed from three junctions that do not agree well (residuals 5 to 12 m before the second pass); low confidence.

100 ft. Part 1: White Horse Pike from Warrick Av to Evesham Av, New Ashland Rd (Ashland Avenue), Gill and Pincus (arbitrary names). Part 2: inset above the heavy line, White Horse Pike, Warrick Av and Lapierre Av at Davis Rd (borough's north end, 'See Map of Barrington').

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 of the Magnolia atlas of March 1925, at 100 feet to the inch, covers the south-eastern part of the borough. Evesham Avenue runs along the top with Pincus Street and King running off it; White Horse Pike runs from Evesham Avenue diagonally down to Evergreen Avenue at the bottom. West of the Pike are the eastern ends of Washington, Lafayette and Jefferson Avenues at Cumberland Avenue, platted in narrow lots with a few dwellings, and at the bottom left Magnolia Avenue with Wilbur Avenue and Harley Avenue, lined with small dwellings. Along White Horse Pike are scattered frame dwellings, a garage and a kennel. A row of houses lines the south side of Evesham Avenue east of King. The borough limit with Clementon Township crosses the sheet twice, and most of the land east of the Pike and south of the limit is open, with a few scattered houses. Water pipes and hydrants are drawn along Evesham Avenue and White Horse Pike. The sheet overlaps sheet 5 along Evesham Avenue and sheet 2 on the west.
notes: King is modern King Street South and Pincus St is King Street North; the two meet Evesham Avenue East about 15 m apart.
Magnolia Avenue / Wilbur Avenue was rejected (10.5 m) and the bottom of the sheet has no control point.
Harley Av is not in OpenStreetMap under that name.
100 ft. Evesham Av south along White Horse Pike to Evergreen Av; King St, Pincus St; Cumberland, Washington, Lafayette, Jefferson Avs; Magnolia Av, Wilbur Av, Harley Av at bottom left. One part.
